snippet:
> For AI client integration (Claude Code, Cursor, etc.), connect to the MCP server at https://docs.bigcommerce.com/_mcp/server.
# MCP Server Overview
> Connect AI agents to BigCommerce storefronts using the Model Context Protocol (MCP). Search products, manage carts, and hand off to checkout through natural language.
An MCP server implements the Model Context Protocol so AI agents — like Claude, Cursor, and others — can discover and call tools over a standard protocol. In practice, an MCP server exposes a set of functions that agents can call to accomplish real-world tasks.
The BigCommerce MCP server lets AI agents interact with a BigCommerce storefront using purpose-built commerce tools. Agents can search products, manage a shopping cart, and hand off to checkout — all through natural language.
## Available tool sets
| Tool set                                                      | Authentication                                              |
| ------------------------------------------------------------- | ----------------------------------------------------------- |
| [B2C Storefront](/developer/api-reference/mcp/storefront/b2c) | Guest and logged-in customer shopping flows                 |
| [B2B Storefront](/developer/api-reference/mcp/storefront/b2b) | Authenticated Buyer Portal user, gated per buyer permission |
Both tool sets are served from the same MCP endpoint, and B2C tools aren't exclusive to B2C stores: the catalog, cart, and checkout tools stay available to every session on a B2B-enabled store too, including guests — that's how a B2B store serves unauthenticated shoppers. The B2B tool set adds the Buyer Portal–specific tools (shopping lists, quotes) on top of that, gated per store by B2B Edition and per tool by the authenticated buyer's permissions. Logged-in B2C shoppers and B2B buyers both authenticate the same way — see [Connecting with session sync](#connecting-with-session-sync-stencil-storefronts) below.
## Prerequisites
* A BigCommerce store with an active storefront
* Node.js version 18 or higher (for `npx mcp-remote`)
## Enable MCP on your store
You must be a **store owner** to enable MCP on a store.
#### Open MCP settings
In the BigCommerce control panel, go to **Settings**. Under **API and MCP**, select **MCP**.

#### Enable Storefront MCP and accept the terms
On the **MCP** page, turn on the **Storefront MCP** toggle. Review and accept the terms of service to enable the MCP server for your store.

snippet:
> For AI client integration (Claude Code, Cursor, etc.), connect to the MCP server at https://docs.bigcommerce.com/_mcp/server.
# Docs MCP Server
The docs site exposes a **Model Context Protocol (MCP) server** that AI tools can search and reference. Once connected, your AI tool can answer questions like *"How does the BigCommerce checkout API work?"* by pulling directly from the docs.
> **Docs search only**
>
> This server lets your AI tool search and reference the BigCommerce documentation. It can't read or change your store, orders, catalog, or account settings. If you're looking for an MCP server that interacts with your storefront, see the [BigCommerce MCP Server](/developer/api-reference/mcp/overview). For everything else, use the [REST and GraphQL APIs](/developer/api-reference).
**`BigCommerce docs MCP server`**
```text title="BigCommerce docs MCP server" showLineNumbers={false}
https://docs.bigcommerce.com/_mcp/server
```

**For a single project**, click the **Copy page** dropdown in the upper right of any docs page and select **Connect to Claude Code**, or copy it from here:
```bash showLineNumbers={false}
claude mcp add --transport http docs-bigcommerce-com https://docs.bigcommerce.com/_mcp/server
```

> For AI client integration (Claude Code, Cursor, etc.), connect to the MCP server at https://docs.bigcommerce.com/_mcp/server.
# Store Management MCP
> Connect an MCP-compatible AI agent to your BigCommerce store to manage catalog, pricing, inventory, and promotions, to look up and refund orders, and to read store details.
Store Management MCP lets an AI agent — Claude, Cursor, ChatGPT, or any other Model Context Protocol (MCP)-compatible client — work directly with your BigCommerce store's catalog, pricing, inventory, orders, promotions, and store profile. This guide covers how an administrator turns on access, how to connect a client, and how to use the tools available in the closed beta.
> **Beta access**
>
> Store Management MCP is in an invite-only closed beta and isn't available by default. To request access, submit the form on the [Commerce AI Labs](https://www.commerce.com/ai-labs/) page. Some capabilities are deliberately limited during this phase; see [Beta limitations](#beta-limitations) for details.

1. In the control panel, go to **Settings → API and MCP → MCP**. You can also search for "MCP" from the **Settings** page.

AI agents.

### Server address
Each store has its own MCP address:
```text showLineNumbers={false}
https://api.bigcommerce.com/stores/{store_hash}/mcp
```
Point your MCP client at the address for the store you want to connect. Because the address identifies the store, the connection flow has no separate store picker.
### Authentication
Connections use OAuth 2.1 with PKCE. Your MCP client registers itself automatically, so there's no client ID or client secret to create or manage.
When you connect, your client sends you to the standard BigCommerce login. Your agent never sees or holds your BigCommerce password, session, or any other credential. If your login normally uses two-factor authentication or single sign-on, it works the same way here.
The scopes assigned to your BigCommerce user (see [Grant a user access](#grant-a-user-access-to-connect-an-agent)) determine which tools your agent can see after you sign in. Every tool call is checked against those scopes on the server, on every request — nothing your agent sends is trusted to establish its identity or permissions.
#### Claude Desktop
1. Go to **Settings → Connectors** and select **Add custom connector**.
2. Paste your store's address: `https://api.bigcommerce.com/stores/{store_hash}/mcp`

title: docs.bigcommerce.com/developer/api-reference/mcp/webmcp
snippet:
> For AI client integration (Claude Code, Cursor, etc.), connect to the MCP server at https://docs.bigcommerce.com/_mcp/server.

WebMCP is a browser standard that lets a website tell an in-browser AI agent what it can do. A site exposes a set of tools, and the agent calls them as structured functions through `document.modelContext`.
On BigCommerce, WebMCP is available on your storefront through a partnership with Cloudflare. It exposes your store's shopping tools to browser-based agents, so shoppers who use an AI assistant can search your catalog, review products, build a cart, and get a checkout link on your store. You don't need to edit your theme or write code.

Once WebMCP is active on your store, a shopper's browser agent can handle requests like:
* "Find a lightweight jacket in my size under \$150."
* "Show me the top 5 bestsellers in Hoodies."
* "What goes well with this jacket?"
* "Add the black one in medium to my cart."
The agent searches your catalog, compares options, adds the best match to the cart, and returns a checkout link. The shopper then reviews the order and completes checkout on your storefront.
## How it works
### Delivery
When WebMCP is enabled, Cloudflare adds a single script tag to your storefront's HTML responses at the edge. The tag references a small bridge script served from your storefront's own domain. Nothing else on the page changes.
**`Injected script tag`**
```html title="Injected script tag" showLineNumbers={false}
<script type="module"
src="/.webmcp/bridge.js"
data-packs="c2pa,mcp-server-client"
data-mcp-url="/api/mcp"></script>
```
* `data-packs` lists the tool packs to activate.
* `data-mcp-url` is the path to your store's MCP server.
The bridge script runs in the shopper's browser and checks whether the browser supports WebMCP. If it does, the bridge registers your store's tools with `document.modelContext.registerTool`. If it doesn't, the script exits and the page behaves as it did before.

**Shopping tools: synced from your server-side MCP.** If server-side MCP is enabled on your store, the tools it exposes are synced to WebMCP automatically. WebMCP and server-side MCP use the same set of shopping tools, so you don't manage two sets of tools. Server-side MCP serves agents that connect to your store directly. WebMCP serves agents that work in the shopper's browser.

title: Build AI Shopping Agents with BigCommerce Storefront MCP
snippet:
[**BigCommerce Storefront MCP**](https://docs.bigcommerce.com/developer/api-reference/mcp/overview) is now available to every store on the platform. Any live, transacting store can opt in starting now.

MCP, or [**Model Context Protocol**](/blog/model-context-protocol/), is an open standard that lets AI agents like Claude, Cursor, and others discover and call tools over a common protocol. Think of it as the interface layer between a language model and the real world. Instead of generating text about products, an AI can search your catalog, build a cart, and hand a shopper off to checkout.
BigCommerce’s Storefront MCP server gives AI agents purpose-built commerce tools to do exactly that: interact with a BigCommerce storefront through natural language on behalf of any shopper.

The B2C Storefront MCP supports the full guest shopping flow end to end. An AI agent can search your product catalog by keyword, retrieve product details and available variants, build and manage a cart, and generate a checkout URL to hand off to the shopper when they’re ready to buy.
The experience is conversational throughout. A shopper describes what they want, the agent finds relevant products, helps them make decisions, and gets them to checkout without navigating a traditional browse-and-filter experience.

Paired with conversational search (also [available to opt in today](https://www.commerce.com/ai-labs/)), this creates a shopping experience that mirrors how customers actually think, not how catalogs are structured.

Storefront MCP is available to any BigCommerce store today. To enable it, log in as a store owner and go to **Settings → Early Access** in your BigCommerce control panel. For everything you need to connect your first agent, see the full technical documentation in the [**BigCommerce developer docs**](https://docs.bigcommerce.com/developer/api-reference/mcp/overview).

title: Storefront Session Sync
snippet:
The BigCommerce MCP server supports session sync for Stencil storefronts. After syncing, the MCP session is linked to the shopper’s existing browser session — carrying their login state, cart, and identity context into the AI agent without exposing cookies.
## How session sync works
Stencil maintains shopper state through `HttpOnly` browser cookies. Because the AI agent backend runs on a separate host from the storefront, those cookies cannot reach it directly.
Session sync bridges this gap using a short-lived opaque token:
1. **Stencil generates a token** — The storefront calls the `generateSessionSyncToken` GraphQL mutation. The token is a one-time opaque token linked to the shopper’s current session, valid for 60 seconds.
2. **The token is passed to the agent** — Your storefront customization passes the token to the AI agent backend (for example, via a chat widget initialization payload).
3. **The agent includes the token at MCP initialization** — The agent passes the token in the `X-Bc-Storefront-Sync-Token` header when initializing the MCP connection.
4. **MCP redeems the token** — The MCP server validates and atomically consumes the token, retrieves the linked storefront session, and builds an MCP session scoped to that shopper.
From this point on, tool calls run in the context of the shopper’s session — their cart, login state, and (if B2B is enabled) their company and permissions. See [Storefront Tools](https://docs.bigcommerce.com/developer/api-reference/mcp/storefront/tools) and [B2B Tools](https://docs.bigcommerce.com/developer/api-reference/mcp/storefront/b2b) for how each uses the synced session. Catalog, cart, and checkout are the base tool set and work the same way for guests, logged-in customers, and company (B2B) buyers; the Buyer Portal–specific tools (shopping lists, quotes) are the extension on top, and always require this session to be active.
### Sequence diagram
## Generating a sync token
Call the `generateSessionSyncToken` GraphQL mutation from the Stencil storefront page. The mutation is nested under the [`mcp`](https://docs.bigcommerce.com/developer/api-reference/graphql/storefront/mutations/mcp) mutation namespace. This must be called from a browser session — server-to-server calls are blocked.
Generate sync token
```
mutation GenerateSessionSyncToken {  mcp {    generateSessionSyncToken {      result {        token      }      errors {        ... on Error {          message        }      }    }  }}
```
